chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: 'That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) disliked eating meat with the skin (or hide) of the animal.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (referring to Imam Ali)
key_terms.اللَّحْمَ بِالْحَيَوَانِ: Meat with the skin/hide of the animal
key_terms.كَرِهَ: Disliked (expressing a recommended aversion, not prohibition)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) dislike regarding the consumption of meat?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the preference of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the consumption of meat with the skin or hide (*lahm bi-l-hayawan*), a practice often associated with the pre-Islamic Arabs. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *taharah* (purity) and the refinement of dietary habits as a reflection of spiritual cleanliness, distinguishing it from mere legal permissibility.
